title: SAML XML parser hardening and remove legacy crypto shims
creator: Priya Khandelwal
description:
Summary:
We discovered multiple security and reliability risks in the SAML/SSO stack during a dependency audit: an outdated XML parsing flow in the saml-adapter that allows entity resolution (XXE risk in certain edge paths), transitively pinned OpenSSL 1.1.x in several base images, and an old JWT/OAuth library with lax token validation behavior for nonce/alg header edge-cases. This ticket consolidates remediation work: replace or harden the XML parser used by the SAML adapters, upgrade OpenSSL in our runtime base images to 3.1.x where feasible, migrate JWT libraries to the community-vetted maintained fork, and retire the last crypto shims that were added for OpenSSL ABI compatibility.

Goals:
- Eliminate XXE/DTD processing surface in SAML flows and add targeted fuzzing/tests.
- Move platform base images and the core SSO service to OpenSSL 3.1.x (or vendor-backed equivalent) and validate no runtime regressions.
- Standardize on a maintained JWT library with strict header/alg validation and implement additional unit/integration tests.
- Remove legacy crypto compatibility shims and document migration steps for Dedicated/Private customers that rely on older ABIs.

Scope/out-of-scope:
In-scope: saml-adapter (go/python microservice), runtime base images used by hosted/Dedicated, CI/infra changes to build OpenSSL 3.1, JWT library upgrade in auth-service, test coverage additions, canary rollout.
Out-of-scope: large-scale TLS policy rework, customer-specific on-prem upgrades (these will be tracked as follow-up tasks with dedicated change windows).
acceptance_criteria: SAML adapter no longer parses external entities and has XXE test coverage (unit + integration)
OpenSSL bumped to 3.1.x in runtime base images and runtime smoke tests pass across linux/glibc images
Auth service uses the new JWT library and rejects tokens with mismatched alg/crit headers per spec
All legacy crypto shims removed from repo and a migration guide created for Dedicated/Private customers
Security review completed and signed off by Security team (link in 'links')
Canary deployment executed (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with latency/cpu/memory dashboards green and rollback plan validated
updates: 2026-02-11: Triage meeting with Security, Auth, and Infra. Initial risk assessment indicates XXE exposure in a low-frequency path. Decided to treat as P1 due to potential data sensitivity.

2026-02-18: Dependency scan produced SBOM; found OpenSSL 1.1.1 in three base images and golang-jwt v3.x pinned in auth-service. Identified transitive xml parser (python defusedxml not consistently used).
2026-02-25: PoC created to disable entity resolution in saml-adapter by switching to lxml with resolve_entities=False. Early tests pass locally; performance overhead <1.5% on median parse time.

2026-03-02: Built OpenSSL 3.1 base image candidate and ran runtime unit tests. Two failing integrations (client cert mutual TLS and a custom cipher fallback) require small code changes—tracking in ENG-36120 as dependency.

2026-03-06: Opened GH PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/saml-adapter/pull/4523 (XML hardening), https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/881 (jwt migration), https://github.com/redwood-inference/base-images/pull/217 (openssl 3.1 image).
2026-03-10: Security review scheduled 2026-03-15; created migration doc for Dedicated customers and notified Solutions Engineering for outreach.
2026-03-12: Integration smoke on the canary cluster (5%) started; slight increase in p99 latency observed for one endpoint—performance team investigating batching interaction with new parser.
